evaluated_findings.title: Insecure Deserialization: Untrusted pickle loading
evaluated_findings.explanation: Python's `pickle` module can instantiate arbitrary Python classes and invoke callable objects during deserialization, making untrusted pickle streams inherently unsafe.
evaluated_findings.proposed_patch:
--- a/routes/upload.py
+++ b/routes/upload.py
@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@
- obj = pickle.loads(decoded)
+ obj = json.loads(decoded)

evaluated_findings.title: SQL Injection: Dynamic formatted query execution
evaluated_findings.explanation: Dynamic string interpolation inside a SQL query allows attackers to alter query logic via malicious input, bypassing authentication or reading confidential database records.
evaluated_findings.proposed_patch:
--- a/routes/users.py
+++ b/routes/users.py
@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@
- cursor.execute(f"DELETE FROM logs WHERE id = {raw_id}")
+ cursor.execute("DELETE FROM logs WHERE id = %s", (raw_id,))

evaluated_findings.title: Weak Cryptography: Insecure hash algorithm MD5
evaluated_findings.explanation: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken algorithms susceptible to collision and preimage attacks. Upgrading to SHA-256 or Argon2 ensures collision resistance.

evaluated_findings.explanation: Hardcoded sensitive keys and access tokens committed to version control can be harvested by attackers or unauthorized contributors to gain access to cloud infrastructure and APIs.
